claims.claim_text: On May 18, 2025 (the Closing Date), Discover Financial Services merged into Capital One and Discover Bank merged into Capital One National Association (CONA). Discover's businesses constituted approximately 21% of total assets and 20% of total net revenue as of and for the year ended December 31, 2025.
claims.rationale: Named, dated, material counterparty merger with quantified materiality. Discover Financial Services was an SEC-reporting entity (CIK 0000091576) prior to closing; merger should be corroborated in counterparty filings (8-K cessation, post-effective amendments, S-8 succession filings).

claims.claim_text: Through the acquisition of Discover, Capital One acquired the Discover Network, the PULSE Network, Diners Club International and Network Partners (collectively, the 'Global Payment Network'). The Global Payment Network processes transactions and earns fees from network participants; Global Payment Network volume was $401,775 million in 2025.
claims.rationale: Operating-status claim about ownership and active operation of named payments networks (Discover, PULSE, Diners). External corroboration should appear in network-participant counterparties' filings.

claims.claim_text: Total deposits were $475,771 million as of December 31, 2025, up 31% from $362,707 million as of December 31, 2024, reflecting the acquired Discover deposit base and organic growth.
claims.rationale: Quantified balance-sheet metric for a bank holding company. Deposit balances at CONA are also reported quarterly to the FDIC via Call Report (FFIEC Call Report) — but that registry is not plumbed in our M-source catalog. Cross-check via 10-Q sequence and merger-closing 8-Ks. Note: this is operational/balance-sheet, not GMV-style headline.

claims.claim_text: Net charge-off rate decreased by 9 basis points to 3.30% in 2025 compared to 2024 (3.39%). The 30+ day delinquency rate decreased by 39 bps to 3.59% as of December 31, 2025. Net charge-offs were $13,102 million in 2025, up 22% from $10,748 million in 2024.
claims.rationale: Quantified consumer-credit charge-off rate trajectory — exactly the kind of disclosure Calibration Heuristic 11 targets. The framework's bar (per cohort calibration) is that consumer-credit-quality assertions don't have a clean registry analog; CFPB consumer complaint database is not plumbed. M-side check is limited to internal consistency across COF's own filings and the absence of widening loss-rate without forward-reserve commentary.

claims.claim_text: Allowance for credit losses increased by $7.2 billion to $23.4 billion as of December 31, 2025 compared to December 31, 2024, primarily driven by the Discover acquisition. Allowance coverage ratio was 5.16% as of Dec 31, 2025 (vs 4.96% Dec 31, 2024).
claims.rationale: Material reserve build directly attributed to the acquisition. Should be corroborated in 8-K acquisition-day day-1 CECL 'double count' reserve disclosure under ASC 326 (PCD vs non-PCD allowance) and in subsequent 10-Qs.

claims.claim_text: Capital One's Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio was 14.3% as of December 31, 2025 (up 80 bps from 13.5% at Dec 31, 2024). Based on 2025 supervisory stress test results, Capital One's stress capital buffer requirement for the period Oct 1, 2025 through Sep 30, 2026 is 4.5%.
claims.rationale: Federal Reserve-determined stress capital buffer is publicly announced by the Fed (DFAST results, typically June-August). Capital ratios are filed quarterly with the Federal Reserve (FR Y-9C). The stress buffer announcement should be corroborated by COF 8-K disclosure (typical practice for large BHCs).

claims.claim_text: Discover, prior to closing, entered into a December 2020 consent order with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) related to certain private student loan servicing practices. As a result of the Transaction, Capital One and CONA now have certain going-forward obligations with regard to these matters.
claims.rationale: Named, dated regulatory consent order with an SEC-reporting predecessor (Discover Financial Services). Should be in Discover's pre-closing 10-K filings (CIK 0000091576).

claims.claim_text: In December 2025, the OCC issued a report of preliminary findings of its ongoing supervisory review, in accordance with Executive Order 14331 'Guaranteeing Fair Banking for All Americans,' affecting Capital One.
claims.rationale: OCC supervisory findings are not directly registered to a public M-source we have plumbed. EO 14331 references in EDGAR fulltext provide a sanity check on the existence of this executive order and whether other banks reference it.
